exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________() lazily pairs items from iterables in parallel; when equal lengths are required, strict=True turns a silent truncation bug into ValueError.

reveal.text: zip() lazily pairs items from iterables in parallel; when equal lengths are required, strict=True turns a silent truncation bug into ValueError.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ common safe mapping pattern is dict(zip(ids, values, strict=True)).

reveal.text: A common safe mapping pattern is dict(zip(ids, values, strict=True)).

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ zip() stops at the shortest iterable, which can hide missing data.

reveal.text: Plain zip() stops at the shortest iterable, which can hide missing data.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ *pairs to zip() expands the sequence of pairs into separate iterable arguments, effectively transposing rows into columns.

reveal.text: Passing *pairs to zip() expands the sequence of pairs into separate iterable arguments, effectively transposing rows into columns.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ points = [(1, 2), (3, 4)], xs, ys = zip(*points) produces separate x and y tuples.

reveal.text: For points = [(1, 2), (3, 4)], xs, ys = zip(*points) produces separate x and y tuples.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________() returns tuples and is lazy; convert the outputs only when a concrete list is actually required.

reveal.text: zip() returns tuples and is lazy; convert the outputs only when a concrete list is actually required.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(iterable, start) yields index-value pairs without maintaining a manual counter.

reveal.text: enumerate(iterable, start) yields index-value pairs without maintaining a manual counter.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ enumerate(lines, start=1) when user-facing line numbers should begin at one.

reveal.text: Use enumerate(lines, start=1) when user-facing line numbers should begin at one.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ start argument changes only the counter, not which elements are consumed.

reveal.text: The start argument changes only the counter, not which elements are consumed.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ a comprehension with multiple for clauses, the clauses appear in the same order as equivalent nested for loops.

reveal.text: In a comprehension with multiple for clauses, the clauses appear in the same order as equivalent nested for loops.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: [__________ for batch in batches for x in batch if x > 0] flattens one level and filters in one expression.

reveal.text: [x for batch in batches for x in batch if x > 0] flattens one level and filters in one expression.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ the for clauses from right to left is a common mistake; translate the comprehension back into nested loops to verify ordering.

reveal.text: Reading the for clauses from right to left is a common mistake; translate the comprehension back into nested loops to verify ordering.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ dict comprehension writes key: value before the for clause and is useful for building lookup tables from objects.

reveal.text: A dict comprehension writes key: value before the for clause and is useful for building lookup tables from objects.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: {__________: user for user in users} creates a lookup where users_by_id[user_id] returns the matching User object.

reveal.text: {user.id: user for user in users} creates a lookup where users_by_id[user_id] returns the matching User object.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ keys that are unique; repeated keys silently keep the last value encountered.

reveal.text: Choose keys that are unique; repeated keys silently keep the last value encountered.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(iterator, default) returns the next item or the default instead of raising StopIteration when the iterator is exhausted.

reveal.text: next(iterator, default) returns the next item or the default instead of raising StopIteration when the iterator is exhausted.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________((user for user in users if user.active), None) is a compact first-match idiom.

reveal.text: next((user for user in users if user.active), None) is a compact first-match idiom.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ the second argument, next() raises StopIteration when no match exists.

reveal.text: Without the second argument, next() raises StopIteration when no match exists.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ := operator assigns a value as part of an expression so a computed value can be tested and reused without calling the function twice.

reveal.text: The := operator assigns a value as part of an expression so a computed value can be tested and reused without calling the function twice.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ chunk := file.read(8192): process(chunk) reads once per loop iteration and stops on an empty result.

reveal.text: while chunk := file.read(8192): process(chunk) reads once per loop iteration and stops on an empty result.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ assignment expressions when they reduce duplication; forcing them into already dense expressions can hurt readability.

reveal.text: Use assignment expressions when they reduce duplication; forcing them into already dense expressions can hurt readability.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ leading * in a call expands an iterable into positional arguments for the target callable.

reveal.text: A leading * in a call expands an iterable into positional arguments for the target callable.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ dimensions = (640, 480), resize(*dimensions) calls resize(640, 480).

reveal.text: If dimensions = (640, 480), resize(*dimensions) calls resize(640, 480).

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ expanded element count and order still need to match the callable's positional parameters.

reveal.text: The expanded element count and order still need to match the callable's positional parameters.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ leading ** in a call expands a mapping into keyword arguments, and ** inside a dict display merges mapping entries from left to right.

reveal.text: A leading ** in a call expands a mapping into keyword arguments, and ** inside a dict display merges mapping entries from left to right.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(*args, **options) combines stored positional and keyword arguments in one call.

reveal.text: train_model(*args, **options) combines stored positional and keyword arguments in one call.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ names must be strings, and duplicate argument assignment can raise TypeError in function calls.

reveal.text: Keyword names must be strings, and duplicate argument assignment can raise TypeError in function calls.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ displays can unpack mappings with **, and later entries override earlier values for the same key.

reveal.text: Dictionary displays can unpack mappings with **, and later entries override earlier values for the same key.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: {**__________, **environment} lets environment-specific values override defaults.

reveal.text: {**defaults, **environment} lets environment-specific values override defaults.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ the unpack order reverses which mapping wins on duplicate keys.

reveal.text: Reversing the unpack order reverses which mapping wins on duplicate keys.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(..., key=...) can return a tuple so Python compares multiple fields lexicographically in priority order.

reveal.text: sorted(..., key=...) can return a tuple so Python compares multiple fields lexicographically in priority order.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________=lambda user: (user.team, -user.score) sorts team ascending and numeric score descending within each team.

reveal.text: key=lambda user: (user.team, -user.score) sorts team ascending and numeric score descending within each team.

prompts.placeholder: __________ works for numeric descending fields; for more complex mixed directions, a stable multi-pass sort can be clearer.

reveal.text: Negating works for numeric descending fields; for more complex mixed directions, a stable multi-pass sort can be clearer.
